lines: Title: Users may be unable to view contacts and Speed Dial entries in Microsoft Teams, Outlook desktop and mobile
User impact: Users may be unable to view contacts and Speed Dial entries in Microsoft Teams, Outlook desktop and mobile.

More info: Affected users may observe missing contacts, blank or grey placeholder entries, or Speed Dial entries that can't be re-added. This behavior may occur across Microsoft Teams desktop and web experiences, Outlook Mobile, and Outlook desktop.

More specifically, this issue impacts in-tenant contacts created in Microsoft Teams using the Notify when available presence notification option. Some older contacts may also be impacted under specific circumstances.

Current status: We’re progressing with deploying the code fix to repair the remaining affected contacts on a user basis. The deployment is ongoing and expected to complete by Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

Scope of impact: Some users attempting to view contacts and Speed Dial entries in Microsoft Teams, Outlook desktop and mobile may be impacted. This information may be updated as our investigation continues.
Start time: Friday, September 25, 2026, at 7:30 AM UTC

Root cause: A problem with a contact-processing component had incorrectly separated some PBCs from their associated profiles when specific contact information wasn't explicitly stored, causing affected contacts to appear as blank.

lines: Title: Admins can't identify who deleted a Viva Engage community or its Microsoft 365 Group in Microsoft Entra ID audit logs
User impact: Admins couldn't identify who deleted a Viva Engage community or its Microsoft 365 Group in Entra ID audit logs.
More info: Impact applied to deletions initiated from both the Viva Engage web experience and the Viva Engage app in Microsoft Teams.

Admins who needed to identify who deleted a specific community or group during the affected period could have opened a Microsoft support case with the deletion date and group/community details so support could trace the initiating user through service-side logs.

Final status: After identifying additional options to expedite remediation, we've confirmed that all three phases of our fix have deployed earlier than expected. We've validated its efficacy and ensured that users who delete Viva Engage or Microsoft 365 groups are now logged in Microsoft Entra ID audit logs.
Scope of impact: This issue prevented all admins from identifying who deleted Viva Engage communities or their connected Microsoft 365 Group in Microsoft Entra ID audit logs.
Start time: Friday, July 10, 2026, at 2:05 PM UTC
End time: Wednesday, October 21, 2026, at 4:30 PM UTC

Title: Users may be unable to connect to multiple Microsoft 365 services
User impact: Users may have been unable to connect to multiple Microsoft 365 services.
Final status: This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents.

The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.

Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration. We will provide a full post-incident report once our review is complete.

More info: Features of the Microsoft 365 services below that interact with Exchange Online and email services were impacted. Elements of those services that do not depend on interaction with Exchange Online remained functional.

- Exchange Online: Users may be unable to access their mailbox using Outlook on the web, Outlook desktop (MAPI), Exchange ActiveSync (EAS), or REST-based connections, and email delivery may be delayed.
- Microsoft 365 admin center: Admins may be unable to load some admin center pages.
- Microsoft 365 apps: Users may be unable to view their recently used files.
- Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center: Multiple services including Cloud Update, Cloud Policy, and Inventory are affected.
- Microsoft 365 Education: Features including Assignments, Reading Progress, and Speaker Progress may be impacted.

- Microsoft Copilot 365: Users may be unable to load Copilot Chat or receive responses in the web and desktop apps, and Copilot experiences may be unable to access work data such as email, calendar, and files.

- Microsoft Defender for Office 365: Some Defender for Office 365 experiences that rely on Purview DLP/Information Protection signals may experience delays or failures in policy evaluation and governance action enforcement. Admins/SOCs may experience delays or failures when accessing NHI features that rely on Data Classification Sensitivity Labels, including Tenant Metrics, Policy, and Data Usage, across the Identity, OAuth, and App Governance pages in the Security portal on Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.
- Microsoft Defender XDR: Users may be unable to load Microsoft Defender portal pages or solution tabs.

- Microsoft Fabric: Users may encounter failures when exporting reports with sensitivity labels to PDF or PowerPoint, when updating artifacts with sensitivity labels, or opening pbix with sensitivity label in Power BI Desktop. As a workaround, users can remove the sensitivity label from the affected item to complete the operation, if their organization's data protection policies allow it.

- Microsoft Graph: API requests that access Exchange Online data, such as mail, calendar, and contacts, may time out and prevent users from managing Teams, Channels, Membership, Apps management and send activity notifications using Graph API.
- Microsoft Intune: Scenarios including device enrollment, device check-in, and device compliance policies may have been intermittently impacted.
- Microsoft Planner: Users are experiencing Plan and Task operation reliability issues.

- Microsoft Power Apps: Users may be intermittently unable to sign-in to the Power Apps or Field Service mobile apps. Affected users may be able to utilize Power Apps or Field Service on the web as a way to circumvent impact, and users who are already signed in can potentially avoid impact by not signing out, clearing app data, or reinstalling while the issue is ongoing. Microsoft Power Apps and Microsoft Power Automate Flows, apps, data refreshes and connectors that rely on Microsoft Graph data were intermittently failing.

- Microsoft Purview: Multiple Purview services including Authorization, auto-labeling, Data Loss Prevention (DLP) across Microsoft 365 services, Communication Compliance, Information Protection label and auto-labeling policies, Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and Data Classification are impacted, and users may be unable to open or load Microsoft Purview portal pages or protected content. Audit searches, protected content creation, eDiscovery tasks such as search and export, Data Classification and On Demand Scan features may also be impacted.

- Microsoft Teams: Most of the core functionality including joining calls, meetings, group chats, and channel messages are not impacted. Scenarios that depend on Exchange Online, including Calendar related failures with scheduling, invites, viewing, and meeting edits. Creation of Live or Virtual events fail. Failures with Copilot responses for outlook, calendar, or M365 files, read history, or adding to new chats. Navigating to App chats, adding new contacts or syncing contacts in settings fail. Standard channels are working fine but users may experience the inability to create or delete private or shared channels.
- Microsoft To Do: The app may not load, and users may see operation failures.
- Power BI: All users may intermittently be unable to export reports with MIP sensitivity labels to PDF in Power BI.

- SharePoint Online: Some users may experience issues when sharing SharePoint Online files with people outside their organization, where external sharing is permitted by both organization-level and site-level settings. Additionally, features that depend on Exchange Online may be impacted. Accessing files stored directly in SharePoint Online remains functional.
- Universal Print: Users may encounter errors submitting print jobs or using admin features.
- Windows 365: Customers who have configured their tenant and Cloud PCs to use Microsoft Purview Customer Key for Windows 365 Cloud PCs may have users who are unable to connect to their Cloud PCs.
Scope of impact: This issue may have affected users attempting to access the affected Microsoft 365 services.
Start time: Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 4:20 PM UTC
End time: Friday, November 13, 2026, at 4:10 PM UTC

Preliminary root cause: While our analysis of the underlying root cause is ongoing, we’ve determined that this incident was caused by a failure in the systems responsible for establishing connections to the Exchange Online service. Specifically, traffic shifts during standard network maintenance and upgrades exposed a latent bug causing a rapidly increasing number of requests to queue for processing. As this accumulated, the affected servers exhausted their available processing capacity and could no longer accept new connections, resulting in widespread service access failures.
Next Steps:
- For a more comprehensive list of next steps and actions, please refer to the Post Incident Report document that will be created for this event.
We'll provide a preliminary Post-Incident Report within two business days and a final Post-Incident Report within five business days.

Title: Users may be unable to connect to multiple Microsoft 365 services
User impact: Users may be unable to connect to multiple Microsoft 365 services.

More info: Features of the Microsoft 365 services below that interact with Exchange Online and email services are impacted. Elements of those services that do not depend on interaction with Exchange Online remain functional.

- Exchange Online: Users may be unable to access their mailbox using Outlook on the web, Outlook desktop (MAPI), Exchange ActiveSync (EAS), or REST-based connections, and email delivery may be delayed.
- Microsoft 365 admin center: Admins may be unable to load some admin center pages.
- Microsoft 365 apps: Users may be unable to view their recently used files.
- Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center: Multiple services including Cloud Update, Cloud Policy, and Inventory are affected.
- Microsoft 365 Education: Features including Assignments, Reading Progress, and Speaker Progress may be impacted.

- Microsoft Copilot 365: Users may be unable to load Copilot Chat or receive responses in the web and desktop apps, and Copilot experiences may be unable to access work data such as email, calendar, and files.

- Microsoft Defender for Office 365: Some Defender for Office 365 experiences that rely on Purview DLP/Information Protection signals may experience delays or failures in policy evaluation and governance action enforcement. Admins/SOCs may experience delays or failures when accessing NHI features that rely on Data Classification Sensitivity Labels, including Tenant Metrics, Policy, and Data Usage, across the Identity, OAuth, and App Governance pages in the Security portal on Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
- Microsoft Defender XDR: Users may be unable to load Microsoft Defender portal pages or solution tabs.

- Microsoft Fabric: Users may encounter failures when exporting reports with sensitivity labels to PDF or PowerPoint, when updating artifacts with sensitivity labels, or opening pbix with sensitivity label in Power BI Desktop. As a workaround, users can remove the sensitivity label from the affected item to complete the operation, if their organization's data protection policies allow it.

- Microsoft Graph: API requests that access Exchange Online data, such as mail, calendar, and contacts, may time out and prevent users from managing Teams, Channels, Membership, Apps management and send activity notifications using Graph API.
- Microsoft Intune: Scenarios including device enrollment, device check-in, and device compliance policies may have been intermittently impacted.
- Microsoft Planner: Users are experiencing Plan and Task operation reliability issues.

- Microsoft Power Apps: Users may be intermittently unable to sign-in to the Power Apps or Field Service mobile apps. Affected users may be able to utilize Power Apps or Field Service on the web as a way to circumvent impact, and users who are already signed in can potentially avoid impact by not signing out, clearing app data, or reinstalling while the issue is ongoing.

- Microsoft Purview: Multiple Purview services including Authorization, auto-labeling, Data Loss Prevention (DLP) across Microsoft 365 services, Communication Compliance, Information Protection label and auto-labeling policies, Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and Data Classification are impacted, and users may be unable to open or load Microsoft Purview portal pages or protected content. Audit searches, protected content creation, eDiscovery tasks such as search and export, Data Classification and On Demand Scan features may also be impacted.

- Microsoft Teams: Most of the core functionality including joining calls, meetings, group chats, and channel messages are not impacted. Scenarios that depend on Exchange Online, including Calendar related failures with scheduling, invites, viewing, and meeting edits. Creation of Live or Virtual events fail. Failures with Copilot responses for outlook, calendar, or M365 files, read history, or adding to new chats. Navigating to App chats, adding new contacts or syncing contacts in settings fail. Standard channels are working fine but users may experience the inability to create or delete private or shared channels.
- Microsoft To Do: The app may not load, and users may see operation failures.
- Power BI: All users may intermittently be unable to export reports with MIP sensitivity labels to PDF in Power BI.

- SharePoint Online: Some users may experience issues when sharing SharePoint Online files with people outside their organization, where external sharing is permitted by both organization-level and site-level settings. Additionally, features that depend on Exchange Online may be impacted. Accessing files stored directly in SharePoint Online remains functional.
- Universal Print: Users may encounter errors submitting print jobs or using admin features.
- Windows 365: Customers who have configured their tenant and Cloud PCs to use Microsoft Purview Customer Key for Windows 365 Cloud PCs may have users who are unable to connect to their Cloud PCs.

Current status: We’re seeing encouraging recovery progress in Europe, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected Microsoft 365 infrastructure. Japan remains comparatively more stable, while North America is also improving; however, some users may still experience intermittent issues as recovery actions continue.

We're focused on addressing the remaining areas of disruption and improving service consistency across affected regions. Reducing email queues and backlogs remains a priority, and the extended 48-hour email timeout window remains in place to help protect delayed messages as delivery catches up.

At this time, we have no evidence of malicious activity associated with this incident. We will continue to treat this with urgency until full mitigation, and we will share a full Post-Incident Report with root cause and defense-in-depth actions after mitigation is complete.

Scope of impact: Some admins that attempted to create mail-enabled security groups in the Exchange admin center or Microsoft 365 admin center may have been affected.

lines: Title: Some users may have experienced delays or failures receiving chat messages in Microsoft Teams desktop client
User impact: Users may have experienced delays or failures receiving chat messages in Microsoft Teams desktop client.
More info: Affected users may have experienced delays receiving messages in the Microsoft Teams desktop client and delays receiving notifications on Microsoft Teams mobile apps.
As a workaround, users may have been able to use Microsoft Teams on the web to access messages without delay.

Final status: We’ve completed the reversion of the service change responsible for the impact and confirmed that new instances of the issue are no longer occurring. Previously affected users who continue to experience residual impact can restart the Microsoft Teams desktop client to restore functionality, while remaining affected clients are expected to recover automatically. In addition, we’ve received confirmation from a number of affected users that impact has been remediated.
Scope of impact: Impact was specific to some users receiving chat messages through the Microsoft Teams desktop client.
Start time: Tuesday, November 10, 2026, at 1:16 PM UTC
End time: Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 10:15 AM UTC

Root cause: A recent service change caused Microsoft Teams desktop client registrations to be unexpectedly removed without prompting the client to promptly re-register, preventing real-time message delivery which resulted in delays.
Next steps:
- We're reviewing our update procedures to better identify similar issues during our development and testing cycles.
This is the final update for this event.
Title: Some users may experience delays or failures receiving chat messages in Microsoft Teams desktop client
User impact: Users may experience delays or failures receiving chat messages in Microsoft Teams desktop client.
More info: Affected users may experience delays of several minutes before messages appear in the desktop client.
As a workaround, users may be able to use Microsoft Teams on the web to access messages without delay.

Current status: We’ve identified that a recent service update is causing some Microsoft Teams desktop registrations to be unexpectedly removed. When this occurs, the affected desktop client isn’t notified that it needs to re-register, preventing real-time message notifications from being delivered and causing messages to appear only after the client performs a periodic synchronization. We’re proceeding with reverting the responsible update to restore normal message delivery.
Scope of impact: Impact is specific to some users receiving chat messages through the Microsoft Teams desktop client.
